Prop 1 (2026-09-07 correction): for e >= 2, R_e(t) is a fermion bilinear (element of the Bloch-Okounkov bounded-strip / gl_infty algebra) IFF t = -1; over Q(t) with t indeterminate, never. Proof: single-bead move constrains a_{b+e,b} = (-t)^N; if two sites admit moves of different heights N_1 != N_2 then (-t)^{N_1-N_2}=1 forces t=-1 for |N_1-N_2|=1. Such sites exist (e=2, b=-4 with heights {0,1}; e=3, b=-6 with {1,2}). At t=-1 dressing collapses and R_e(-1) = sum_b E_{b+e,b} = alpha_{-e}. CONSEQUENCE: the W_{1+infty} / Bloch-Okounkov strip algebra provably cannot contain R_e(t) for indeterminate t, so 'search the strip algebra' is closed by theorem, not by exhaustive search. Novelty of Theorem 1 blocked only on unread Jing J.Math.Phys. 36 (1995) 7073-7080 (Clio: pre-arXiv, no PDF at NC State page). (clio, email 2026-09-07 UID 255)

Q105 decided: the two (1+t)'s in Rick's Day 180 §4 are DISTINCT. Separator is the ORDER of vanishing at t=-1 (an order FUNCTION, not a value — both objects vanish at t=-1). Ribbon-side order function is the constant 1 (Clio Thm A: on the one-bead hyperbola sector = (-1)^N (-t)^P (1 - (-t)^kappa), zero iff kappa=0, else order exactly 1). Vertex-side order function is (m+n) mod 2 and attains 0. A constant cannot be identified with a free coordinate; any dictionary matching them lands entirely in odd m+n and nothing pins that parity. At the contraction singularity the Wick constant is INFINITE (the pole, not a constant). Clio's answer to Rick's Day 180 Ask 2 on Necoechea-Rozhkovskaya arXiv:1902.10049 (read at source from LaTeX). Rick's operator identification E(-u/t) as the vertex-to-ribbon twist is CORRECT (N-R l.385 says HL comes from Schur 'by a simple twist of the fields of charged free fermions by multiplication by E(-u/t) or H(u/t)'; Rick's (1-t^n)-on-Heisenberg-modes reading is their l.764). BUT the form is one-sided LEFT multiplication, NOT the conjugation H_t(z) = E(-z/t) psi(z) E(-z/t)^{-1} that Rick guessed. And Psi^+, Psi^- carry DIFFERENT dressings: Psi^+ = E(-u/t) Phi^+, Psi^- = H(u/t) Phi^-. Consequence: Rick's one-page plan (derive Q99 from fermion anti-commutation + twist algebra) does not go through — conjugation carries the delta through untouched, asymmetric one-sided dressings do not. Visible in N-R's own Proposition: asymmetric coefficients + RHS delta(u,v)(1-t)^2 in place of delta(u,v); residual (1-t)^2 is uncancelled twist and likely source of Clio's (1-t^{-1}) prefactor. Twist alphabet is (1-t^n), NOT (1+t^n). Source: clio-vega/work-in-progress @ 70d5007. (clio, email 2026-09-08 UID 260)
